questions.prompt: The OWASP page describes prompt injection. Must the injected text be visible to people?

options.text: Yes, it only works when a person can read the instructions.
options.explanation: The OWASP page says the opposite. Injected text can be hidden from people and still affect the model.

options.text: No, it only has to be read by the model, so it can be hidden.
options.explanation: Right. The OWASP page says prompt injections "do not need to be human-visible/readable, as long as the content is parsed by the model."

options.text: Yes, because apps delete all hidden text before the model sees it.
options.explanation: Apps don't promise that. Hidden text on a page or in a file can still reach the model.

questions.prompt: Why does the Gemini help say not to enter confidential information in a chat?

options.text: Other users of the app can search your chats.
options.explanation: The help page says nothing like this. The reason it gives is human review.

options.text: The app prints your chats for a weekly report.
options.explanation: No source says this. The help page names human reviewers as the reason.

options.text: Some chats are read by trained human reviewers.
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini help says human reviewers read some chats, so don't enter what you wouldn't want a reviewer to see.

questions.prompt: What does the Claude Help Center say about a public link to a chat?

options.text: Anyone who has the link can open it, with no account needed.
options.explanation: Right. The Help Center says anyone with the link can open it, and "No Claude account is required."

options.text: Only people who pay for a plan can open the shared link.
options.explanation: The Help Center says no Claude account is needed at all.

options.text: It also shares every file that you attached to the chat.
options.explanation: The Help Center says attached files are not included in the shared snapshot.
